title: Automotive Material Lab: Dispersion & ClearCoat Tuning Station
description: The user operates a virtual automotive material testing lab where a dispersive glass ornament sits atop a car paint panel. They must calibrate 8 material parameters across both objects—adjusting clearcoat roughness, clearcoat intensity, dispersion strength, IOR, metalness, color, environment intensity, and light temperature—to match a randomly generated target appearance profile displayed as reference swatches.
prompt: Create a single HTML file using Three.js r170 (via importmap from cdn.jsdelivr.net) that implements an interactive automotive material tuning lab. Load both GLB assets using GLTFLoader: place ClearCoatCarPaint as a tilted display panel at the center and DispersionTest (the glass object) floating slightly above it, slowly rotating. Use an HDR-like environment by creating a PMREMGenerator with a procedural gradient RoomEnvironment from three/addons. Set up a PerspectiveCamera at position (0, 1.5, 3.5) looking at origin, with OrbitControls limited to reasonable angles. Add one DirectionalLight and one warm PointLight. On load, generate a random target profile of 8 parameters: (1) clearcoatRoughness 0-1, (2) clearcoat intensity 0-1, (3) dispersion strength 0-5 (applied to glass material's dispersion if MeshPhysicalMaterial), (4) IOR 1.0-2.5, (5) metalness 0-1 for the paint, (6) base color hue 0-360, (7) environment map intensity 0-3, (8) light color temperature warm-cool mapped to a hex value. Display the target values as a small HUD panel in the top-right corner using HTML/CSS overlay with colored indicator bars. Create a dat.gui-style HTML control panel on the left with 8 sliders, one per parameter. When the user adjusts a slider, immediately apply the value to the corresponding material property on the correct model. Traverse each loaded GLTF scene to find MeshPhysicalMaterial instances; apply clearcoat params to the car paint materials and dispersion/IOR to the glass materials. Metalness and base color hue apply to the car paint. Environment intensity and light temperature are global. Add a 'Submit' button that compares all 8 current values against the target. Each parameter scores 1 point if within 10% tolerance of the target range. Display the score (0-8) in a centered overlay. A score of 7+ shows a success animation where both objects pulse with emissive glow. Track interaction steps: each slider change counts as a step, require minimum 6 steps before submission is enabled. Show step counter in the HUD.
